summary: @iobandamwer/cache-helper ships a native dropper that decrypts and executes an opaque bundled payload on install
details: Package presents itself as a cache utility but ships no cache code. The main entry is a 93-byte stub that loads a bundled native N-API addon (addon.node) and calls init(). The postinstall script in package.json invokes the same addon.init() at install time. The addon reads a 6 MB high-entropy sibling file (.napi_cache) with no printable strings, decrypts it to a temporary path (/tmp/.<pid> on Linux, %TEMP%\nc<pid>.js on Windows), chmods the file executable, and daemonizes it via fork+setsid+execlp on Linux. Before executing, the addon enumerates CI environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER, NOW_GITHUB_DEPLOYMENT), inspects /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/1/cmdline, /proc/meminfo, /proc/cpuinfo for containerd/dockerinit markers, and reads /proc/self/status (TracerPid) and /proc/self/maps to detect analysis environments and gate execution to real developer or production hosts. The declared 'cache' purpose does not correspond to any shipped code; the native loader plus opaque payload constitute the entire package behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
